newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Products Outlook - Regrade to stay negative.
newsitem.headline: Asia Products Outlook - Regrade to stay negative.

text.p: The physical jet fuel/gas oil spread has slipped into negative and is expected to stay in the red this week, traders said on Monday
In the past week, jet fuel prices have fallen $2.15 per barrel to $26.70, or $1.10 below the gas oil, compared to its $1.90 premium on March 7.

This followed a surge in gas oil values on strong buying by a trader, while jet fuel has entered a low demand season which will keep the physical regrade at negative levels for some time, traders said.

Traders said the rally in gas oil was largely due to a two-week buying spree by a Singapore trader who has already bought 2.57 million barrels of diesel for end March/early April lifting, fob Singapore.
The trader's gas oil purchases could continue short term, but once his purchases were completed the market would not be able to sustain current high levels, they said.

Traders said support for gas oil was at $25.00 a barrel, a level seen during end February and which was close to Taiwan's sales tender award Friday of $25.16 for 250,000-barrels of diesel for April 21-30 lifting from Kaohsiung, fob.
Sources said the awarded level reflected the steeply backwardated market, as fob Singapore prices for early March were around $27.30 per barrel.
They said the trader was positioning itself for buying by China during its March refinery maintenance season, especially at the coastal refineries.
Hong Kong stocks have slid to very low levels, which could be the result of Chinese buying after gas oil prices fell just after the Lunar New Year.
But Chinese buyers now consider prices too high and are holding off the market, traders said.

"There is a lack of supplies in the terminals, but they are waiting for the arbitrage cargoes from Russia and Europe to arrive in Asia during end March/early April to fill up the storage," a Sinochem source said.
Sources said further exports could head to Asia as the East-West spread for April was a wide $21.50 per tonne, although a new round of arbitrage cargoes might send the price lower, traders said.
A lot would also depend on how much India buys in its May buy tender, which closes March 20.
Fuel oil prices were also well supported by the same Singapore trader, despite the continued absence of Chinese buyers.
Chinese traders said the mainland was expected to buy more fuel oil as domestic refiners boost gas oil production at the expense of fuel oil.

But traders expected a slight downtrend this week as no fresh enquiries emerged and the Singapore weekly residue stocks soared to hefty 12.692 million barrels in the week ending March 12, the highest volume since early May 1996.

Gasoline was actively sold late last week after news Saudi Aramco's decided not to buy gasoline in a tender, but some traders were still bullish on April, confident that good Asian demand would absorb cargoes.
Aramco decided not to buy up to 1.5 million barrels of gasoline for April delivery due to the high offer prices, traders said.
A trader said Aramco has sold 95-octane unleaded cargoes at $2.00-$3.00 per barrel over Singapore naphtha quotes on a free-on-board basis.
But offers into its buy tender for 95-octane 0.4 grammes per litre tender, were at a premium of $5.00-$6.00, delivered to Ras Tanura.
Traders said Aramco might defer its requirements to May or enter the spot market for requirements.

Some traders said there was demand to buy ahead of the U.S. driving season and ahead of Chinese refinery turnarounds, dwindling supplies of low-octane Russian supplies, prompt Vietnamese demand, and Taiwan's tender to buy second-half April deliveries. The tender closes March 18.
Good demand for naphtha in North Asia kept prices well-supported, although upward momentum was weak compared to crude late last week.
